        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Project complete: Latham Street Wastewater Upgrade 🪛
 
What began as a small sinkhole investigation revealed significant deterioration underground: a corroded concrete flume that had been quietly breaking down beneath the reserve for years.
 
The repair became one of our most complex live-network projects to date. Delivered by our contractor <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tw-civil-and-infrastructure?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>TW Civil and Infrastructure</a>, the work required precise coordination of operational teams, careful management of material supply, and very specific site conditions to carry out safely, all while maintaining service levels throughout.
 
Delivered:
 ✅ Old collapsed flume fully removed
 ✅ Modern pipe, new manholes and valve chamber installed
 ✅ Improved network resilience
 ✅ Reserve restoration underway
 
The key to making this work was preparation. A 'flow management' method was trialled back in November to prove the team could execute the full repair without impacting level of service. That investment in planning paid off in the delivery.
 
Thank you to TW Civil and our operational teams for seeing this one through. Napier's wastewater network is upgraded, more resilient and future-ready.</p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Napier City Council today confirmed that recommendations from its first Citizens' Assembly will inform planning for the future of the Napier Aquatic Centre. The council voted in favour of officers now developing a project plan that incorporates the recommendations. This will then inform options for consideration as part of the 2027–37 Long-Term Plan.
 
Napier’s first Citizens’ Assembly, which convened in September 2025, brought together 40 residents selected through a ‘sortition’ process from more than 700 applicants aged 16 and over. Their brief was to recommend what type of aquatic centre would best meet Napier's future needs, and where it should be located. No recommendation on location was made, but the Assembly provided useful direction on what any future site would need to include.
 
For those working in deliberative democracy, this model is worth noting. Rather than running a citizens' assembly as a standalone exercise, we have structured it as the first step in a longer engagement process with outputs feeding into statutory planning. That sequencing gives the Assembly's work a clear purpose. Formal public engagement on Napier’s Long-Term Plan is set for early 2027.</p>
